test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 17 Oct, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following States/Union Territories is NOT a part of Indus River Basin?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sikkim**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indus River Basin covers parts of India, China, and Pakistan, particularly the northern regions.
 
• States like Himachal Pradesh, Ladakh, and Jammu & Kashmir are part of the Indus River Basin.
 
• Sikkim, located in the northeastern part of India, is not part of the Indus River Basin.
 
• The major rivers in Sikkim include the Teesta and Rangeet, which are part of the Brahmaputra River Basin.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indus River Basin:**

 
 
• The Indus River originates from the Tibetan Plateau and flows through India and Pakistan.
 
• It is one of the longest rivers in the world, with a length of approximately 3,180 km.
 
• The basin covers a significant area in the northwestern part of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The major tributaries of the Indus River include Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej.
 
 
 
• **Teesta River:**
 
 
• The Teesta River is a major river in the Indian states of Sikkim and West Bengal.
 
• It originates from the Pahunri (or Teesta Kangse) glacier and flows southward through the Himalayas.
 
• The river ultimately merges with the Brahmaputra River in Bangladesh.
 
 
 
• **Brahmaputra River Basin:**
 
 
• The Brahmaputra River Basin is one of the largest river basins in the world, covering parts of China, India, and Bangladesh.
 
• It spans an area of about 580,000 square kilometers.
 
• The river is known for its strong currents and high water discharge, especially during the monsoon season.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Significance:**
 
 
• The Indus River Basin plays a crucial role in the agriculture and economy of the regions it covers, providing water for irrigation and drinking purposes.
 
• Sikkim, on the other hand, with its rivers like Teesta, supports hydropower projects and agricultural activities in the northeastern region of India.
